newsitem.title: USA: Smith Barney Q3 net up 17 pct - Travelers.
newsitem.headline: Smith Barney Q3 net up 17 pct - Travelers.

text.p: Smith Barney's earnings showed continued strength in the third quarter as net income rose 17 percent to $208.7 million from $177.9 million reported in the 1995 quarter, its parent Travelers Group Inc said.
"Smith Barney demonstrated earnings strength in the quarter, despite the traditionally slower summer months for the securities industry," the Travelers statement said.

"The firm also continues to benefit from ongoing expansion of its products and services, which last quarter included the introduction of client access to no-load mutual funds, an industry 'first' for a full-service brokerage firm."

Smith Barney's return on equity reached 32.2 percent, up from 28.9 percent in the comparable 1995 quarter, as the firm said it continued to produce one of the highest ROEs in the securities industry. Pre-tax profit margins increased to 22.7 percent versus 21.1 percent in the prior year period.

Total revenues, net of interest expense, increased five percent to $1.51 billion, Travelers said. Commission revenues totaled $498.0 million compared with $536.1 million in the 1995 quarter, reflecting lower activity in listed and over-the-counter securities and options.

Smith Barney's annualized retail gross production per Financial Consultant (FC) rose four percent to $334,000, compared with $322,000 in the 1995 quarter, with a sales force of 10,430 FCs working from 450 domestic retail offices.

Asset management fees rose 26 percent to a record $342.3 million, reflecting growth in money market funds, mutual funds, institutional managed accounts, and retail WRAP accounts -- which all represent sources of recurring revenue. At September 30, Smith Barney also had a record level of assets under management of $105.4 billion, up 14 percent from a year ago.
Net interest income reached a record $106.0 million, up 14 percent from $92.6 million in the prior year period.

Investment banking revenues increased 19 percent to $288.5 million compared to the prior year's quarter, reflecting fee income from the firm's second highest level of merger and acquisition advisory activity, as well as strong volume in taxable fixed income underwriting. The firm was the top underwriter of long-term negotiated municipal debt in the quarter, with about a 12.7 percent share of the market.
Principal trading revenues totaled $243.0 million compared with $255.6 million in the 1995 period.

Total expenses, excluding interest, were lower than the 1996 second quarter, and slightly higher than the 1995 third quarter as a result of increases in production-related compensation and other operating expenses.
The firm continues to have one of the industry's lowest ratios of non-compensation expense to net revenues, which was 21.3 percent for the 1996 third quarter.
